issues.title: Figma MCP enabled but OAuth authentication unavailable
issues.description: Codex listed figma-temp and figma-primary as enabled, but neither produced a ready MCP client and the UI reported authentication failure.
issues.root_cause: A remote MCP entry being enabled does not perform OAuth login. Both servers were correctly configured but remained in the Not logged in state; the Codex App did not complete the explicit login flow.
issues.solution: Use the official Codex CLI against the shared config: run `codex mcp login figma-temp` and `codex mcp login figma-primary`, completing each browser authorization with the intended Figma account.
issues.verification: `codex mcp list` reports both Figma servers as enabled with Auth=OAuth. A fresh Codex App session is still required to expose their tools, and account separation must be checked with account-exclusive test files.
issues.prevention: After adding an OAuth HTTP MCP, check `codex mcp list`; if it says Not logged in, run `codex mcp login <server-name>` before restarting the client. Never equate enabled with authenticated.

issues.title: Two Figma MCP servers reused the same browser identity
issues.description: Both figma-temp and figma-primary authenticated successfully, but their whoami calls returned the same temporary-account identity.
issues.root_cause: The second browser OAuth flow reused the Figma account already signed in to the default browser. Separate MCP server names isolate stored credentials, but they do not choose different browser identities automatically.
issues.solution: Log out only figma-primary, switch the default browser to the long-term Figma account, then run `codex mcp login figma-primary` again. Leave figma-temp credentials unchanged.
issues.verification: After restarting the Codex App, parallel whoami calls confirmed figma-temp and figma-primary have different emails and the expected account prefixes. The temporary account handle is Ran; the long-term account handle is zju.
issues.prevention: Before authorizing a second server for the same OAuth endpoint, switch the browser to the intended account. Verify both identities with whoami in fresh clients before creating canonical assets.

issues.title: Hermes acceptance video and production preview used different API conditions
issues.description: The release-gate WebM showed a healthy Dashboard and Hermes whole-character motion, while the user's 3194 page did not match it. The initially linked WebM also failed to load in the app.
issues.root_cause: The release gate intercepted auth, research-object, and ingestion requests with successful fixtures, but 3194 had been started without `API_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3188`; its real server-side requests fell back to port 3001 and rendered `无法加载工作台 / 请求失败 500`. An already-open `next start` tab could additionally retain old JS/CSS after rebuild. The Markdown handoff referenced a local WebM filesystem path rather than an HTTP media URL.
issues.solution: Start 3194 with the verified local preview API on 3188, then run and record an acceptance browser with zero API interceptions. After each production rebuild, open a fresh cache-busted Dashboard URL. Serve ignored visual evidence through a bounded localhost HTTP server instead of a local media path.
issues.verification: The unmocked 3194 browser loads Ada Researcher and the real preview RO without the 500 error; Hermes reports idle/ready with reduced motion false, exercises six actions in 18 seconds, and moves across a 33x23px range. The final 35.8-second 1440x900 WebM uses zero API interceptions and has no console errors. Dashboard and video URLs both return HTTP 200, with the video served as `video/webm`.
issues.prevention: A release video must use the same API origin and data path as the handed-off preview. Before visual delivery, run one zero-interception browser probe that rejects Dashboard error copy, records the real body/state/renderer/action trajectory, and only then records video. Never ask for acceptance from a tab that survived a production rebuild; publish evidence over HTTP and verify status/content type.

issues.title: Hermes motion video forced animation while the real Codex browser honored Windows reduced motion
issues.description: The corrected Dashboard and video used the same API data, but the user still saw a static Hermes while the Playwright recording moved.
issues.root_cause: Windows SystemParametersInfo reported ClientAreaAnimationsEnabled=false, so the Codex Chromium browser exposed prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Hermes deliberately returned a still motion sample, skipped the WebGL renderer, and disabled CSS whole-character motion. The acceptance recorder explicitly forced reducedMotion: no-preference, so it did not represent the user's browser environment.
issues.solution: Add one explicit Hermes motion preference resolver. The default continues to honor the system, while ?hermes-motion=full opts into full mesh, CSS whole-character actions, and pointer input. Scope reduced-motion CSS suppression to stages that have not explicitly selected full motion.
issues.verification: With Playwright still emulating prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the system URL remains fallback with zero travel, while ?hermes-motion=full reports rig ready/input true, performs eight actions in 20 seconds, moves the actor 25.39px with a 34.08px size delta, and enters engaged state on pointer input.
issues.prevention: Visual acceptance must run once with the user's real reduced-motion condition. Any recorder override must be disclosed and paired with an equivalent product preference; data attributes or test-only media emulation cannot substitute for the user's rendered result.

issues.title: Real arXiv PDF failed before MiniMax extraction
issues.description: The real 24,671,920-byte arXiv 2009.06045 PDF first failed malware policy and then entered parser review, despite being a legitimate paper that parsed correctly outside the production pipeline.
issues.root_cause: The artifact scan applied the byte sequence ../ to every format instead of only ZIP archives, and the controlled parser limit was 20MB. After those fixes, direct string matching still rejected valid MiniMax evidence quotes because PDF extraction changed whitespace, punctuation and line-break hyphenation.
issues.solution: Apply traversal detection only when ZIP magic is present while retaining global EICAR/PE checks; raise the bounded parser input to 50MB; match evidence by exact text, whitespace equivalence, then a unique NFKC alphanumeric canonical sequence, always persisting the original manuscript substring and locator.
issues.verification: The real paper completed ECS upload, parsing, MiniMax extraction, review, confirm and version commit. Five supported fields have original-source character locators, while unsupported reproducibility remains explicitly missing. Focused artifact/worker tests preserve ZIP traversal rejection and the 50MB+1 boundary.
issues.prevention: Production ingestion acceptance must include a real large PDF, exact source-locator verification and explicit missing fields. Generic byte heuristics must be gated by the file format they describe.

issues.title: MiniMax workspace guide output repeatedly failed the strict result contract
issues.description: A real Dashboard workspace.guide task called MiniMax-M3 successfully three times but ended failed with the structured-output retry limit.
issues.root_cause: The prompt named fields without defining their exact types or allowed object keys and did not enumerate current authorized target IDs. MiniMax returned useful prose using title/description, a question array for needsMoreInformation, and open-task actions when no such target was available. Identical retries had no new constraint and repeated the mismatch.
issues.solution: Keep the strict guard and server authorization unchanged. Supply membership-scoped SDF core fields to the model, state the exact JSON shape and forbidden keys, require a boolean needsMoreInformation, and enumerate the only allowed task/RO IDs for navigation.
issues.verification: After a full ECS deployment, a real browser Dashboard submission succeeded in about 40 seconds, accurately identified the complete RO, the missing reproducibility evidence and duplicate diagnostic drafts, and returned only authorized RO/task navigation links.
issues.prevention: Structured AI prompts must specify exact types, exact allowed keys and runtime allowlists; retries must not be treated as evidence that an underspecified contract will self-correct.

issues.title: Deployed Hermes appeared static and did not guide the real creation workflow
issues.description: In real production use, Hermes did not visibly idle or respond, did not swim to key form locations, and did not explain what the user should enter at creation and SDF-editing milestones, despite motion-focused release videos passing.
issues.root_cause: The user's Windows browser still resolves system reduced motion and the full-motion URL override is neither persisted nor exposed as a product control. Separately, only Dashboard registers the real assistant presentation and drawer; creation/edit routes render a neutral stage. Route guidance hard-codes only the first title/problem target, has no field-completion progression, and several displayed Explain/Draft/Check actions have no consumer on the current route.
issues.solution: Make HermesWorkspaceStage the sole motion-preference owner, persist the explicit full/reduced choice, expose an accessible enable-motion control, and pass the resolved value into the adapter and rig. Keep a real route-owned assistant drawer on creation/edit pages, advance guide targets from title/import and selected SDF fields, and render only actions that have a consumer; Explain now shows field-specific guidance locally.
issues.verification: TDD RED captured the missing persisted preference, unavailable motion control, inert create actions, and static ro-title/sdf-problem targets. GREEN evidence: focused motion 16/16, local and public production-browser creation/edit/motion matrices 6/6, Web 295/295, typecheck, canonical lint, 17-page build, and the 145.6-second Hermes release gate. The release gate measured 5,215 idle-breathing and 58,228 pointer-response changed pixels plus distinct head/torso/tail motion. ECS source hash matches release aa1c8af, restarted Web/API/Worker are healthy, and recent critical-error counts are zero.
issues.prevention: A random-motion video is not a workflow acceptance test. Every Hermes release must be exercised in the actual user media preference and through the uninterrupted creation/editing milestones, with visible controls and route-owned action consumers.

issues.title: Hermes visual-review keyboard menu raced asynchronous scene URL navigation
issues.description: The first production acceptance run passed right-click, long press, fallback and reduced-motion cases but intermittently failed Shift+F10 after a rapid Editor to Review to Editor tab sequence.
issues.root_cause: The visual fixture kept scene state locally while calling asynchronous Next router.replace for the query string. During a rapid Review to Editor return, the browser URL was still editor, so Next treated the second replace as a no-op while the first review RSC request remained in flight. Its eventual commit could race the newly opened context menu.
issues.solution: Keep the fixture's local reducer as the interaction owner and update the same-route view query synchronously with window.history.replaceState. Add a browser contract requiring each Arrow-key scene change to update the query before the next input event.
issues.verification: A deterministic RED assertion observed local state=review while the URL still said editor. After the single navigation-boundary change, the focused regression and full five-case local route suite passed. ECS hotfix b73a9dd deployed with no migration; public full acceptance passed 5/5 and the keyboard scenario passed three additional concurrent repeats.
issues.prevention: For local-only same-route visual controls, do not mix immediate reducer state with an asynchronous server navigation solely to mirror a query parameter. Assert state and URL move atomically before testing subsequent keyboard input.

issues.title: Isolated worktree deployment could not locate cloud sync configuration
issues.description: A confirmed immutable deployment from the Hermes feature worktree stopped before upload because the worktree did not contain the ignored cloud sync configuration file.
issues.root_cause: Deployment configuration is intentionally stored only at the main repository root, while the release command ran from an isolated worktree. The deploy script supports an explicit configuration root, but the first invocation did not set it.
issues.solution: Keep the feature worktree as the release source and set XGS_CONFIG_ROOT to the main repository root for the deployment process. This lets the sync helper locate the existing ignored configuration without copying it into the worktree or exposing its contents.
issues.verification: The first call failed before upload and left the active release, failure marker and candidate tree unchanged. The corrected call materialized the exact clean release, completed the server build and healthy container switch, and passed exact release plus public 5/5 Hermes acceptance.
issues.prevention: When deploying from an isolated worktree, always set XGS_CONFIG_ROOT to the main repository root before dry-run and confirmed release commands; never copy or commit the ignored deployment configuration into the worktree.

issues.title: Ubuntu visual release gates sampled runner-dependent browser timing and mismatched DOM contracts
issues.description: PR #4 passed build, typecheck, lint and unit tests on Ubuntu but exposed runner-dependent slow-pointer sampling, menu geometry, pixel-evidence duration, screenshot-clock speech ordering, a mismatched Hermes loading-state selector and an implicit motion-preference precondition in the production visual gates.
issues.root_cause: The browser case moved only 2px between host-timed waits and sampled one fixed snapshot. SwiftShader RAF cadence could therefore miss the 70ms response peak even though the deterministic interaction model met the slow-motion contract. Separately, Linux and Windows font metrics made the Hermes menu 1-1.5px taller than the design baseline, and the detached-menu cold-start case could position against pre-font geometry because it omitted document.fonts.ready. Ubuntu software rasterization could spend about 28 seconds decoding the 1920px evidence pair and exhaust the generic 60-second test budget during the final full-page evidence screenshot. The Hermes speech-order test also treated completion of two software screenshots as a product clock, so the valid 520ms feedback timer could fire before the second capture returned. The Hermes loading test searched for main[aria-busy=true], although DashboardShell deliberately forwards aria-busy to its data-os-surface=dashboard root. The context-loss test expected the full-motion Retry label without pinning full motion, so an environment reduced-motion preference could correctly expose Enable instead.
issues.solution: Keep the exact 12px/1s >=.05 slow-response contract in the deterministic model test. In the browser, use a still-slow 12px stepped traverse and record the peak plus final pointer coordinate continuously on RAF instead of requiring every host-timed step to cross the threshold. Wait for fonts, two layout frames and menu animation settlement, and allow 2px cross-platform font-metric tolerance below the nominal 24px band while retaining independent zero-overlap and 48px upper-bound gates. Give only the three visible-optical cases a 120-second total evidence budget; do not relax any action-level timeout, perceptual threshold or geometry assertion. Record Hermes action and feedback DOM timestamps with a MutationObserver, retain the immediate no-speech and two-frame real-motion gates, and assert a >=450ms physical-reaction lead independently of screenshot duration. Assert the loading shell through its data-os-surface and aria-busy contract, verify its aria-live child, and wait for the mocked 503 response before inspecting the error DOM. Pin the context-loss case to hermes-motion=full and assert the toggle's active and fallback runtime attributes before checking its accessible Retry name.
issues.verification: The focused interaction model passed 18/18, the fresh production Web build passed, the optical cases passed 10/10, the detached Hermes cold-start case passed 10/10, the event-order case passed 5/5 (15 selections), and the complete production visual release gate passed 72/72. CI run 32959918188 trace recorded slowPeak 0.111 and the expected pointer coordinate before its final evidence-screenshot timeout; run 32961184540 then passed all three optical cases and failed only the obsolete post-screenshot speech absence check. CI run 32962638531 exposed the impossible loading selector; run 32964668644 then passed product release 72/72 and exposed the implicit context-loss motion state. After both corrections, the full local production Hermes gate passed 19 compatible-runtime and 8 product-interaction cases.
issues.prevention: Do not encode perceptual velocity through host-scheduled 2px browser events, block each input step on a transient peak, use screenshot completion as a product clock, assert portal geometry before fonts and animations settle, guess a component's attribute owner from its visual hierarchy, or assert a preference-dependent label without fixing the preference. Put exact time-domain thresholds in deterministic tests; browser gates should record observable RAF, API and DOM event order while preserving independent pixel-motion and physical-overlap checks. Budget software-rendered pixel evidence separately from behavior-level waits.

issues.title: ScanSci auth tunnel exposed the noVNC directory root instead of the client
issues.description: The canonical ScanSci auth tunnel reported the loopback root URL. Opening it showed a websockify directory listing with no CARSI login surface.
issues.root_cause: websockify serves the noVNC static directory at `/`; the interactive remote desktop client is `/vnc.html`. The tunnel script used the directory root both for readiness and operator-facing start/status output.
issues.solution: Use `/vnc.html?autoconnect=true&resize=remote` as the single canonical operator path for readiness, start, duplicate-start and status output. Keep the tunnel bound to 127.0.0.1 and do not expose a public authentication route.
issues.verification: The exact client URL returned HTTP 200 and contained the noVNC client while the auth container was running. The regression test first failed because the old root probe received 404, then the complete auth-tunnel suite passed 21/21 after the path correction.
issues.prevention: Readiness must probe the same complete operator URL that the command prints. A static-directory HTTP 200 is not evidence that an interactive client is reachable.

issues.title: ScanSci Chromium could not start inside the hardened auth container
issues.description: The noVNC and RFB paths connected, but the remote desktop never presented the CARSI login browser.
issues.root_cause: Debian Chromium could not create its inner namespace or setuid sandbox under the deliberately hardened auth container. The entrypoint also started a redundant blank browser, while pinned ScanSci invoked Patchright through channel=chrome without forwarding its configured browser path; the first wrapper attempt was therefore unreachable.
issues.solution: Bind the image's channel=chrome alias to the fixed wrapper, let pinned ScanSci be the sole browser lifecycle owner, and persist its publisher Cookie files rather than claiming a persistent Chromium profile. The wrapper adds --no-sandbox only inside the hardened container, removes conflicting proxy switches, fixes the controlled Squid path, and disables QUIC/non-proxied WebRTC. The auth helper mounts no account Secret, publishes noVNC only on host loopback, and requires HTML plus WebSocket/RFB plus remote process/PID/topology verification.
issues.verification: Regression tests first failed for the unreachable channel alias, old host-network/Secret topology, static-only readiness and missing runtime process contract. Targeted Dockerfile, session, Compose, RFB and runtime suites pass after the change. Production Chromium, CARSI and cookie-state verification is recorded separately in the CURRENT handoff after deployment.
issues.prevention: Trace the exact pinned upstream browser selection path, including channel aliases; do not infer it from config keys. Browser acceptance must prove RFB, the real Chromium argv, PID headroom, network/Secret isolation and the target page. Describe only the publisher Cookie persistence the pinned implementation actually provides.

issues.title: ScanSci auth diagnostics left a Chromium process tree and an IPv6 VNC listener
issues.description: A one-off headless Chromium probe remained inside the old auth helper until it reached 125 of 128 PIDs. Independent review also found x11vnc listening passwordless on IPv6 port 5900 despite the IPv4 loopback listen argument.
issues.root_cause: The diagnostic command had no process-level timeout and its output pipeline did not guarantee Chromium termination. x11vnc enables an IPv6 listener separately unless explicitly disabled.
issues.solution: Use the canonical auth-tunnel stop operation to remove the exact helper and local tunnel, verify that the container and ports 5900/6080 are absent, and add x11vnc -no6 with a regression contract.
issues.verification: Canonical stop reported stopped, a second status read reported stopped, and the remote container plus both listener ports were absent. The focused entrypoint test failed before -no6 and passed after it was added.
issues.prevention: Every server diagnostic subprocess must have an explicit timeout and cleanup path. Auth acceptance must inspect PID usage and both IPv4 and IPv6 listeners before credentials are entered.

issues.title: Passwordless noVNC was reachable from the shared retrieval network
issues.description: Host loopback publication prevented public access, but the auth helper shared retrieval_net with application containers, so a compromised peer could connect directly to passwordless websockify inside Docker.
issues.root_cause: A 127.0.0.1 host port binding constrains only host publication; it does not isolate container peers on the same bridge. Runtime tests had asserted the shared topology instead of proving peer denial.
issues.solution: Make scansci-auth the sole peer on a fixed internal auth_net. Create the network before browser start, atomically install and reload the dedicated Squid listener with one durable rollback and one pending marker, and apply an exact host-input policy that allows xgs-auth0 only to 172.25.0.1:7891 and rejects every other host address and port. Make the Chromium wrapper fail closed when the fixed proxy is absent.
issues.verification: Compose and Squid contracts require the dedicated subnet; runtime verification rejects extra peers and probes proxy success, gateway and ECS-primary SSH denial, raw-direct denial, and legal-service denial of scansci-auth:6080. Failure injection proves the old live config survives before commit, post-commit failure automatically restores and reloads it, and a failed candidate reload follows the same recovery. Production evidence remains required before credentials are entered.
issues.prevention: Treat host port binding and container network isolation as separate controls. A passwordless operator surface must have no untrusted bridge peers, and server acceptance must prove the negative path from a real application container.

issues.title: Expired ScanSci auth helper left a locally live but unreachable SSH forward
issues.description: After the bounded ten-window operator login expired, the browser reported that it could not connect even though the canonical tunnel status still printed running.
issues.root_cause: The remote scansci-auth container correctly exited after the bounded login attempts, but the SSH -N process remained locally identifiable because its control connection was still alive. show_status checked only the recorded process identity, and duplicate start compensated the stale tunnel but returned failure instead of continuing with a fresh helper. An interrupted start could also leave a healthy-looking starting state that a retry accepted without the post-start runtime verifier.
issues.solution: Require status to pass the same HTTP plus WebSocket/RFB readiness gate as start. When an exact owned runner is alive but unreachable, report an explicit non-running state. A subsequent canonical start must stop the recorded runner, remove only the stored-release auth helper, preserve a pending tombstone if that stop fails, and continue to a fresh start after successful cleanup. Only committed running state is idempotent; any observable starting state is precisely removed and recreated through the full verifier.
issues.verification: Production evidence showed a local 6080 listener with failed HTTP/RFB while the remote helper had exited 1 without OOM. A canonical stop/start restored HTTP 200 and RFB_OK. Same-port, cross-port, unreachable-starting and healthy-starting verifier-bypass regressions failed against the old behavior and pass with the candidate; the full tunnel suite passes 32/32 and both code/security reviews are READY.
issues.prevention: Never equate a live SSH control process with a live forwarded application. Status and operator-facing links must use the complete protocol readiness gate, and restart must recover an exact stale lifecycle in one command without broad process cleanup.

issues.title: CARSI request snapshots were written outside the cookie directory used by pinned ScanSci
issues.description: The Zhejiang University session reached ready and survived scansci-legal recreation, but three bounded institutional DOI canaries all returned stable not_found.
issues.root_cause: OpenScience copied the 0600 publisher Cookie into a request-local session-snapshot/carsi_cookies directory and exposed that path through carsi_cookie_dir. Pinned ScanSci PDF 1.11.0 ignores that key and constructs its Cookie path exclusively as cache_dir/carsi_cookies, while the generated cache_dir pointed to an empty output/cache directory. The persistent validator read the original Cookie successfully, but every acquisition worker missed its safe snapshot.
issues.solution: For requests with an accepted session snapshot, point the generated cache_dir at that request-local snapshot root so pinned ScanSci reads snapshot/carsi_cookies. Preserve the separate output cache for OA-only requests, the original source Cookie, the bounded copy, and all ownership, mode, symlink and containment checks.
issues.verification: A production diagnostic proved one safe snapshot Cookie, institutional sources enabled, original session ready, but snapshot COOKIE_LOAD=0 and COOKIE_SESSION_VALID=0; a constructor proof showed pinned ScanSci uses cache_dir and ignores carsi_cookie_dir. The regression test then failed with upstream_unavailable on the old config and passes after the two-line path correction; all 95 ScanSci legal tests pass with six Windows/POSIX boundary skips. PR #28 merged and canonical release 2019f8a proves cache_dir now equals the request snapshot, but the strict institutional PDF canary exposed the separate browser-runtime issue recorded as issue-017.
issues.prevention: Validate third-party configuration keys against the exact pinned implementation rather than a plausible mock contract. A persistent-session gate is incomplete until the request-local worker proves it can load the copied Cookie from the path the pinned client actually reads.

issues.title: ScanSci treated a publisher 403 page as CARSI success while the legal image had no browser runtime
issues.description: The auth helper published ready and saved a safe Cookie artifact, but after exact deployment the session became auth_required and both persistent and request-local Cookie validation returned false. Real ScienceDirect article and PDF probes returned 403 through requests, CPU Chromium, ECS direct egress and the optional home tunnel.
issues.root_cause: Pinned scansci-pdf 1.11.0 declares federated login successful when the browser reaches any publisher URL outside login keywords or has more than three Cookies, so a ScienceDirect 403 page is a false positive. Its institutional try_carsi source is browser-backed, while the production scansci-legal image contains neither Chromium, Patchright nor Xvfb; the fixed requests homepage validator also requires HTTP 200 and cannot establish browser entitlement.
issues.solution: Use a product-owned strict login gate that promotes staged Cookies only after a fixed non-OA Zhejiang University canary returns allowlisted institutional PDF evidence. Put CPU Chromium, Patchright and private Xvfb in a separate no-Secret browser worker with opposite-direction input/output tmpfs mounts; directly fix the wrapper/proxy launch with no bundled fallback, return browser-originated status/MIME/URL/hash proof, and kill the complete process group on timeout or failure.
issues.verification: Production evidence: active/public release 2019f8a, one safe JSON Cookie file with five valid-shaped records, state auth_required generation 16, request cache_dir equal to its snapshot, persistent and snapshot loads false, ScienceDirect article/PDF HTTP 403 with no SSO redirect, and zero PDF magic through requests and Chromium. The user approved the strict browser design; architecture review closed three Important boundary issues, and the reviewed inline TDD plan is commit cf114e7. Implementation, CI, redeploy, one new operator login and a real institutional PDF journey remain pending.
issues.prevention: Never use URL shape, Cookie count or redirect absence as proof of institutional entitlement. Acceptance must execute the same browser-backed source as production and require bounded PDF evidence before ready is persisted.

issues.title: Official ScanSci cleanup stopped Squid and a cacheless rebuild exposed truncated proxy downloads
issues.description: After removing the rejected browser firewall unit and its systemd drop-ins, Squid became inactive. The active release kept serving but a later cacheless ScanSci image build failed first with proxy connection refused and then with hash mismatches on different partially downloaded PyPI wheels.
issues.root_cause: The removed firewall unit had been a systemd requirement of Squid; stopping it propagated a stop before the stale drop-in was removed, and cleanup did not reassert Squid active/listener state. Clearing 29.21 GB of inactive BuildKit cache then forced the next immutable release to reacquire the full official Python closure through an intermittently truncating home-tunnel parent. Pip's --require-hashes correctly rejected every incomplete object.
issues.solution: After deleting the obsolete dependency, daemon-reload and restart Squid, then require active plus exact 127.0.0.1:7891 and 172.24.0.1:7891 listeners and a real proxied request. Keep hash enforcement. Split both generated ScanSci and BGE locks into one hash-complete requirement block per pinned package, install each block with --no-deps --require-hashes and a fixed five-attempt loop, then verify the complete environment. A transport failure therefore retries only the current package without accepting an unlisted hash.
issues.verification: Squid returned active and a proxied request returned HTTP 200 with no 172.26 listener. PR #50 CI 33653209566 passed. Exact ECS build recovered the formerly truncated hf-xet wheel, installed all pinned ScanSci/BGE packages and built the fixed BGE revision. Canonical release 80db41e passed Parser, BGE CPU, core/search 34/34 and 2/2, 17 tools, Worker MCP, real OA, public CAS and retention. Post-cleanup active/public matched, Squid/listeners and containers were healthy, old runtime/eval/dangling counters and build cache were zero, and disk was 50G/148G with 92G available.
issues.prevention: Any systemd dependency cleanup must verify the dependent service after daemon-reload, not only its configuration file. Do not delete all inactive build cache without ensuring pinned dependency layers can be deterministically rebuilt; immutable downloads must retain --require-hashes and use bounded per-package retries rather than accepting new hashes after a transport failure.
